title: Pullback comparison of ordinary sheaf Hom complexes and source shifts
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $g:X'\to X$ a morphism of schemes, and $F=g^*:\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_{X'})$ the exact constant-coefficient small-etale inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply $F$ termwise to unbounded cochain complexes. Write $H(E,I)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{A_X}(E,I)$ [def-pur-hom-complex], and $H'$ for the same construction on $X'$, using sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Use ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and its canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. For any complexes $E,I$ there is a canonical chain map
$$c_{E,I}:F H(E,I)\longrightarrow H'(FE,FI).$$
For each $n,p\in\mathbf Z$, its composite with the projection to $\mathcal Hom(FE^p,FI^{p+n})$ is the transpose, under the tensor-Hom adjunction of $\operatorname{Mod}(A_{X'})$ and the symmetry of $\otimes_{A_{X'}}$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], of
$$F(H(E,I)^n)\otimes_{A_{X'}}FE^p\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H(E,I)^n\otimes_{A_X}E^p)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev}_{n,p})}FI^{p+n},$$
where $\mathrm{ev}_{n,p}$ evaluates the $p$-component of a degree-$n$ family of maps. The map $c$ is natural contravariantly in chain maps of $E$ and covariantly in chain maps of $I$.
Use cohomological shifts $(E[m])^p=E^{p+m}$ with differential $(-1)^m d_E$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let
$$s_{E,I,m}:H(E[m],I)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(E,I)[-m]$$
be the signed source-shift map whose degree-$n$, $p$-component sends a family $f$ to $(-1)^{mn}f^{p-m}$; let $s'$ denote the corresponding map on $X'$. For every integer $m$ one has the equality of chain maps
$$s'_{FE,FI,m}\circ c_{E[m],I}=c_{E,I}[-m]\circ F(s_{E,I,m}),$$
under the termwise identification $F(E[m])=(FE)[m]$. No boundedness, flatness or injectivity is required, and neither $c$ nor preservation of infinite products by $F$ is asserted to be an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); agent extension to ordinary Hom complexes using the differential in sites-cohomology.tex, section-hom-complexes, and signed source reindexing.

proof.text: By the inverse-image proposition, $F$ is additive and is canonically the ringed-topos module pullback for $A_X\to A_{X'}$. Hence applying $F$ to each differential gives a complex: $F(d^{p+1})F(d^p)=F(0)=0$. Additivity gives $F((-1)^m d)=(-1)^mF(d)$ for every integer $m$, so termwise pullback identifies $F(E[m])$ with $(FE)[m]$, including the differentials. In the following, $[U,V]$ denotes sheaf Hom and $[a,b]$ its map given by precomposition with $a$ and postcomposition with $b$.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact); additive specialization and the cohomological shift convention

proof.text:
For module sheaves $U,V$, define $q_{U,V}:F[U,V]\to[FU,FV]$ by transposing $F[U,V]\otimes FU\xrightarrow{\sim}F([U,V]\otimes U)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev})}FV$. The inverse tensor comparison supplies the first arrow; the closed adjunction and symmetry supply the transpose. These are morphisms of module sheaves. For $a:U'\to U$ and $b:V\to V'$, naturality of the tensor comparison and adjunction gives
$$[Fa,Fb]q_{U,V}=q_{U',V'}F[a,b].$$
Explicitly, after tensoring with $FU'$ and evaluating, both sides are $F$ of the map $[U,V]\otimes U'\to V'$ sending $(h,u')$ to $b(h(a(u')))$. The adjunction is injective on morphisms, so the two arrows agree. Evaluation also identifies the transpose of a sum or negative with the sum or negative of the transposes, since $(h+k)(u)=h(u)+k(u)$ and $(-h)(u)=-h(u)$. These are direct consequences of the cited adjunction, not an additional pullback-Hom theorem.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), constructed by evaluation using Tags 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor)

proof.text:
Put $P^n=H(E,I)^n$ and write $\pi_{n,p}:P^n\to[E^p,I^{p+n}]$ for its product projections. Define
$$t_{n,p}=q_{E^p,I^{p+n}}F(\pi_{n,p}):FP^n\to[FE^p,FI^{p+n}].$$
The product universal property gives a unique $c^n:FP^n\to H'(FE,FI)^n$ with these components. Its $p$-component has exactly the evaluation transpose in the statement: moving $F(\pi_{n,p})$ across the tensor comparison gives $F$ of projection followed by evaluation, namely $F(\mathrm{ev}_{n,p})$. The products exist sectionwise by the Hom-complex definition, with the universe bound already fixed in the statement. This constructs an arrow into the target product and never identifies $F$ of a product with a product.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), termwise product definition; evaluation construction from sites-modules Tag 0GMX

proof.text:
To check the chain-map equation, test against every target product projection. The defining differential gives
$$\pi_{n+1,p}d_H=[1,d_I^{p+n}]\pi_{n,p}-(-1)^n[d_E^p,1]\pi_{n,p+1}.$$
Using the naturality identity of step 2 on these two summands, and additivity of $F$, gives
$$\pi'_{n+1,p}d_{H'}c^n=[1,Fd_I^{p+n}]t_{n,p}-(-1)^n[Fd_E^p,1]t_{n,p+1}
=q_{E^p,I^{p+n+1}}F(\pi_{n+1,p}d_H)=\pi'_{n+1,p}c^{n+1}F(d_H).$$
The product projections determine a map, so $d_{H'}c^n=c^{n+1}F(d_H)$ in every degree. Each equality only involves two summands; no exactness of products is used.

For chain maps $a:E'\to E$ and $b:I\to I'$, the degree-$n$, $p$-component of $H(a,b)$ is $[a^p,b^{p+n}]\pi_{n,p}$. Consequently both sides of
$$H'(Fa,Fb)c_{E,I}=c_{E',I'}F(H(a,b))$$
have component $q_{E'^p,I'^{p+n}}F([a^p,b^{p+n}]\pi_{n,p})$, by step 2. Equality follows from the product universal property. The Hom-complex definition says these componentwise composition maps are chain maps; step 4 says the same for $c$. This proves the asserted naturality in both variables.

Verify also that the stated signed reindexing really is a chain isomorphism. For a degree-$n$ family $f$ in $H(E[m],I)$, put $(s^nf)^p=(-1)^{mn}f^{p-m}$. The component has source $E^p$ and target $I^{p+n-m}$, so belongs to $H(E,I)^{n-m}$. The inverse in degree $n$ sends a family $h$ to $f^r=(-1)^{mn}h^{r+m}$; its two composites are identities. Using $d_{E[m]}=(-1)^m d_E$ and $d_{H(E,I)[-m]}=(-1)^m d_{H(E,I)}$, both $s^{n+1}d(f)$ and $d(s^nf)$ have $p$-component
$$(-1)^{m(n+1)}d_I^{p+n-m}f^{p-m}-(-1)^{mn+n}f^{p+1-m}d_E^p.$$
Thus $s$ is a chain isomorphism. The same computation defines $s'$ on $X'$. These formulas hold for all integers, since only parity is used.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential; agent signed source-shift computation

proof.text:
Finally take degree $n$ and project the proposed compatibility equality to $[FE^p,FI^{p+n-m}]$. On the left the resulting arrow is
$$(-1)^{mn}q_{E^p,I^{p+n-m}}F(\pi^{E[m],I}_{n,p-m}).$$
On the right it is
$$q_{E^p,I^{p+n-m}}F\bigl((-1)^{mn}\pi^{E[m],I}_{n,p-m}\bigr).$$
They agree by additivity of $F$ and of composition. Here the shifted map $c_{E,I}[-m]$ has component $c_{E,I}^{n-m}$, without an extra sign; the differential sign has already been included in step 6. Product projections give the asserted equality of chain maps. The construction used arbitrary terms of $E,I$, so applies to unbounded complexes without flatness or injectivity assumptions.
